en.name: Leo XIII
en.summary: Author of Rerum Novarum, the 1891 encyclical that founded modern Catholic social teaching.
en.body: Leo XIII succeeded Pius IX and, over a twenty-five-year papacy, worked to re-engage the Church with the modern world after decades of confrontation with liberal and nationalist movements. His most influential act was the 1891 encyclical Rerum Novarum, which addressed the condition of industrial workers, defended the right to organise labour unions, and criticised both unrestrained capitalism and socialism — establishing the foundation of what became known as Catholic social teaching. He also encouraged the revival of Thomistic philosophy in Catholic education.
